records.title: EST-inspired computational approaches to event boundary detection
records.reason: Tried the ACM publisher record; no primary full text was available. The title concerns event-boundary detection inspired by event-stream sensors, not language-model inference. Because the linked Nyströmformer relation is not clear and the body could not be checked, retain as borderline pending source access.

records.title: Bounded Reachability&Jailbreak Detection via Contraction-Constrained State Space Models
records.reason: The paper proves robustness certificates for contraction-constrained SSM safety heads and evaluates toxic-comment/jailbreak detection; a contraction penalty improves certified fraction and transfers across safety datasets. Its contribution is provable safety classification, not inference efficiency or sequence-model compression, so the shared SSM lineage is not enough for inclusion.

records.title: NegT2IBench: When Negation Changes the Picture. A Polarity Benchmark for Text-to-Image Models
records.reason: NegT2IBench is a text-to-image polarity benchmark with controlled positive/negative constraints and detector-based scoring, validated with human labels across models. It measures generation adherence, not LLM inference efficiency; the linked VLM paper is only a broad multimodal connection.

records.title: Refinement Buys Intelligibility, Search Buys Identity: What Test-Time Compute Buys in Masked-Diffusion TTS
records.reason: The paper studies inference-time refinement steps and best-of-K search in masked-diffusion text-to-speech, evaluating intelligibility and speaker identity over model sizes and step budgets. It finds the two compute sources help different capabilities. This is speech synthesis rather than LLM/VLM inference, and the linked reasoning-compute family is only an analogy; retain borderline.

records.title: Most-Recent Anchoring with Recurrent Ordering for Time Series Forecasting
records.reason: MARO processes time-series patches from most recent to oldest with a shared recurrent module and evaluates forecasting benchmarks/ablations. It improves forecasting without increasing parameters with longer history, but is not an LLM reasoning/inference method; the linked recurrent-depth reasoning paper is a superficial architectural analogy.
